svg.text: stdx's regular expressions on rebar's other benchmarks against Rust's regex and Go's regexp, on Neoverse-N2
The bars share one logarithmic axis of stdx over Rust regex. The other libraries stand in the columns at the right.
A bar is the median of stdx over Rust regex:
|—| the interval of the median: the jobs' 5th lowest to 5th highest ratio, 97% confidence
searches of rebar's imported definitions, in multiples of Rust regex's speed
against Rust regex: ahead on 50 (2 inside 5%), level on 0, behind on 56 (11 inside 5%) of 106 rows, 106 patterns; geometric mean over
against Go regexp: ahead on 101, level on 0, behind on 5 of 106
Each row is a benchmark of rebar outside its curated set and its tests whose engines name Go's regexp or RE2, under rebar's own model,
pattern and haystack. rebar's author chose them, and no work on stdx has measured them. rebar's README says that they mostly serve to make
Rust's regex crate faster, and rebar's BIAS.md says its benchmarks may favor that crate.

against Go regexp: ahead on 6, level on 0, behind on 9 of 15
A row is ahead or behind where its interval lies above or below 1, and level where it holds 1 inside 5% of 1. A row whose interval holds 1
and reaches past 5% is unclear: its jobs do not settle it. A difference inside 5% is one this chart calls too small to matter, and the
counts still name its direction. A bar ahead or behind inside 5% is drawn lighter, and the shaded band on each panel is 5% of 1.
The columns at the right are stdx's speed over another library's, the median of the jobs. A library has no speed (—) on a pattern that it
refuses, where its answer is not Go regexp's, and where it has no such call.
stdx timed again, last in each round, differed from stdx by at most 19.1% in any job of any row.
